items.title: Get Started
items.text:
Tucker Island is a Discord server in support of Matt, Mikayla, and Tucker. The server is acceptance-based and all members are friends & family. The server is home to a variety of fun features that have been fine-tuned to appeal to everyone. This page contains documentation on every feature and will be updated according to feedback, updates, and new features.

Vefora Economy Court

Redirect

For more information you can visit the tab designated for ourVefora bot.

Vefora is a bot created by @xyb specifically for logging information that takes place in the server. It has documentation on all statistics relating to users, moderative actions, and can be especially helpful in court.

Redirect

For more information you can visit the tab designated for ourEconomy system.

The economy system is built on UnbelievaBoat, a Discord bot marketed specifically for its economy commands and overall system. It's simple in function, and has numerous gambling games you can play to earn yourself more money.

Redirect

For more information you can visit the tab designated for ourCourt system.

Court is a dynamic and fun activity that engages members of Tucker Island. It involves a judge, jury, prosecutor(s), defendant, and lawyer(s). The activity can generally span out to length a few hours, and involes both Criminal and Civil trials according to the server's list of Criminal Charges, and Suable Offenses.

Tip

All text colored blue is a link and can be clicked on!

Post Date

All information is up to date as of 2026-02-23(ISO 8601)

items.title: Economy
items.text:
The economy system is managed by the Discord bot UnbelievaBoat. The economy influences events that happen in the server, roles, and more. If you'd like to go through the commands yourself please refer to:

Notice

Please only use economy-related commands in the designated channels, #economy, and #cell-block.

  • typing / in #economy, pressing the UnbelievaBoat icon and scrolling through.

  • visiting the official command page they provide. The server uses the default prefix, ! for all commands.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: The economy system is simple, this cohesive guide will help you get started earning!

items.title: Earning Money
items.text: Earning money is an essential part of the experience on Tucker Island. It's good to know the basics!

items.title: work
items.text:
You pick up a job in the T-Regime and earn yourself ᛟ17-23. This command is usable every two minutes. 

/work

items.title: crime
items.text:
You can commit a crime in the T-Regime and potentially earn ᛟ600-1250. It's worth mentioning that there is a 60% chance of failure and a fine of 20 - 40%. This command is usable every twenty-five minutes. 

/crime

items.title: rob
items.text:
Allows you to rob another member of the Discord server, taking all the Cash they have. This command does have a chance of a fine, but all parameters of it are unknown. 

/rob <user>

  • <user> - Mention a user to attempt robbing them.

items.title: collect-income
items.text:
You have a government mandated ᛟ100 that you earn every day. This command allows you to recieve that money. For anyone that has a government-related role, you will recieve an additional amount of money on top of the regularly mandated payout. This amount is determined based on the following formula, (<people in server>*100)*0.05. 

/collect-income

items.title: Storing Money
items.text: When your money is stored it ensures other members of the server cannot rob you of your cash.

items.title: deposit
items.text:
Allows you to deposit all or a specific amount of cash into your bank. 

/deposit <amount | all>

  • <amount | all> - You can type a specific amount to deposit, or type all to deposit all the money you have into your bank. Optionally you can just leave it blank and use purely /deposit to deposit all, this method doesn't work with the ! prefix.

items.title: withdraw
items.text:
Allows you to withdraw all or a specific amount of cash into your bank. 

/withdraw <amount / all>

  • <amount | all> - Refer to deposit's explanation as it functions the same.

items.title: Spending Money
items.text: The ability to spend money is an important part of the server as you can buy collectables, and usable items of varying tradability. Some items will be exclusive or limited edition raising their value and encouraging in-server trading (selling). Usable items generally earn you benefits inside specific events, give your roles, or allow for other features.

items.title: store
items.text:
Allows you to view all the items the T-Regime has in market. 

/store [page]

  • [page] - Intakes an integer number, that puts you at the specified store page.

items.title: inventory
items.text:
Allows you to access all the items in your inventory. 

/inventory <user> [page]

  • <user> - Mention and specify which user's inventory you'd like to see, if left blank it'll default to you.
  • [page] - Intakes an integer number, that puts you at the specified inventory page.

items.title: buy-item
items.text:
Allows you to buy an item from the store. 

/buy-item [quantity] <item name>

  • [quantity] - Intakes an integer number, that buys the specified amount.
  • <item name> - Intakes a string value, that buys the item specified.

items.title: sell-item
items.text:
Allows you to sell (trade) an item in your inventory to another member for monetary gain. 

/sell-item <member> [quantity] <item name>

  • <member> - Mention and specify which user you'd like to sell to.
  • [quantity] - Intakes an integer number, that sells the specified amount.

items.title: use-item
items.text:
Allows you to use an item in your inventory. 

/use-item [quantity] <item name>

  • [quantity] - Intakes an integer number, that uses the specified amount.
  • <item name> - Refer to buy-item's explanation as it functions the same.

items.title: Vefora
items.text:
... is a bot made with Tucker Island in mind. It's an automated logging tool for moderators and users alike. Most logs are posted in #public-logs under VEFORA __LOGS. Created by @xyb it's a dependable tool that tracks a large amount of data related to the server.

Common Q&A

Q: Why can't I use some commands that Vefora has? A: Not all commands/information is accessible to the general public. If you'd like to request specific information that you cannot access as a regular user please contact @xyb to submit a data-request.

Q: Am I allowed to privately request data in court? A: No, if participating in court please refer to using a verbal request rather than a private one. This action when used in court counts as using a witness if you decide to pull @xyb up for a testimony in regards to accessing the data desired.

items.title: Court
items.text:
After anticipation a full guide for Tucker Island Court has finally been created. To control how lengthy each page can be the Court section has been split into numerous pages.

Please refer to this Table of Contents to navigate easier, if need be.

  • Court Overview (This page).
  • Offenses
  • Suing Guidelines
  • Court Roles
    • Judge
    • Prosecutor
    • Lawyer
    • Defendant
    • Jury
  • Charges

Disclaimer

Court roles and basic Court charges are due to change overtime is the game evolves. If you personally have any recommendations please refer to the google form.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
Court is an activity in Tucker Island that acts loosely similar to U.S. Court. It includes both Criminal and Civil trials that take place in the server, with verdicts that have interesting or funny charges.

Generally Court involves five major roles. These five include the following:

  1. A judge
  2. The jury
  3. Prosecutor(s)
  4. Lawyer(s)
  5. A defendant (Plaintiff's are also called defendants).

Without these components Court cannot function as intended. It's a party activity that requires the cooperation of numerous members in the server.

items.title: Proceedings
items.text:
First a trial must be established. This means a criminal or civil trial must first be created for Court to commence.

How are trials created?

As we know there are two types of trials: criminal and civil. A criminal trial is created after a member of the server commits a crime according to the list of misdeamenors and felonies. A civil trial is created when a member of the server sues another member in the bounds of our suing guidelines.

When does a trial start?

Trials are scheduled according to when others are free, and when that day & time is reached the trial will be carried out.

How does Court play out?

items.title: Intermission
items.text: Court officially begins when all essential members of the trial join the session. From there, each side will have ten minutes of intermission to organize a game-plan, gather evidence, and review this website if need be. If the trial is a civil one, the prosecutor must state their reason for the trial and what they seek to gain out of it.

items.title: Round Start
items.text:
Both the defendant, and prosecutor will choose a side of a coin. Then the judge will flip a coin to decide who goes first. If the judge is incapable of flipping a coin, they will pick a member of the jury to do so.

The chosen party will begin their statements, claims, and overall argument. They are allowed to bring up witnesses, present evidence, cross-examine, object to the opposing side, challenge their credibility, impeach evidence, request time extensions, and do really anything you'd expect in court. The opposing party is generally not allowed to speak, but lawyers do have the abiltiy to do callouts like, (e.g.) "heresay".

items.title: Round Cycles
items.text: Each round will cap at ten minutes. Throughout the round the jury is allowed to request to speak, and speak into the chat to make comments on the argument and other things. However the opposing side in the trial does not have permission to speak. There are a minimum of four rounds total in a trial. After each round the opposing side gets priority to make their argument for the next. If after the set four rounds a compelling amount of time extension requests, or requests to extend how many rounds there are exist; the judge can add an additional two, four, six, eight (etc.) rounds to the trial.

items.title: Vulnerabilities
items.text:
1. Every round only two witnesses can be brought up.
  2. Evidence submissions are limited to four per round.
  3. Find loopholes in this documentation if you want an advantage on your case.

items.title: Conclusion
items.text:
After all the rounds have played out. The defendant and the prosecutor, plus their accomplices will be unable to talk for the rest of the session. The judge and jury will come to a final consensus on what charges the defendant should face, if any.

Then court will be released and the charges may be applied. The judge can also rule additional proceedings at the end of the trial if they wish to do so. For example, like an extra trial of justifiable paramaters.

items.title: Charges
items.text:
User Generated Charges

You can access all the active user-generated charges here!

The charges that can fall upon the parties in a trial are predominantly user-generated. However there are some preset charges that will never expire in usage. They're rudimentary charges that were meant to set a baseline and serve as a template for user-generated charges.

Jail Probation Tax Audits License Suspension Dunce Ordered Nickname

The recipient of the Jail charge is given the @incarcerated role and is banished from all communication on the server. This excludes a chatroom and voice-chat, the #cellblock and #showers.

Instead of being put into incarceration throughout their sentence, they're allowed to roam supervised by other members under the @probation. If they trip up, their charges will worsen and additional charges may pile on.

This is essential just a fine. A set amount of money, or a percentage is taken from the recipient's total networth with Tucker Isles's economy bot.

The recipient is effectively suspended from monetary gain, using economy channels, and the economy bot.

The recipient gets a shameful role and is put onto display on the Member List menu. Anyone who has the @dunce role is considered a dolt, or a dullard.

Recipient is forced to wear a nickname decided by the judge and jury.

items.title: Suing Guidelines
items.text:
Suing another person is a way to involve the community more in a trial rather than commiting a server offense. Only one party benefits at the end of it, and any civil trial has the chance to backfire on the prosecutor.

Much like criminal offenses there are no hard guidelines to creating a sueable offense. However, it should follow the server's rules and it should be and offense that encroaches on another person's wellbeing in some way.

Examples

  • Someone can be sued if they cause PLACEHOLDER_1 to happen as a direct result of their negligence or recklessness with PLACEHOLDER_2.
  • If anyone breaks a verbal or written agreement with PLACEHOLDER, they can be sued.
  • Someone can be sued if they make false or damaging statements about another person that harm their reputation.

Note: These examples are pretty boring. Not every sueable offense needs to be crazy or wacky but have fun and be creative with what you submit! It makes court more enticing and fun to play. Thank you!

Disclaimer

Any sueable offense shouldn't specify a person in it. Instead it should be able to apply to any two or more people.

items.title: Offenses
items.text:
This page covers the general guidelines to creating an offense in the server.

When making an offense, you don't need to specify the extremity of the charge. Whether that be it's a misdeameanor or a felony the Court and its members will use it appropriately to their own interpretation.

Difference to Sueable Offenses

With sueable offenses, one party benefits from winning the trial. In a criminal offense trial it's either the defendant gets punished or they walk free. It will typically result in more ruthless punishments.

You can make the criminal offense anything you desire so long as it abides by the server's rules.

Examples

  • Someone is commiting a crime when they say the word, PLACEHOLDER.
  • If anyone does PLACEHOLDER they are commiting a crime.
  • Someone is commiting a crime if PLACEHOLDER_1 and PLACEHOLDER_2 happen within ten minutes of each other.

Note: These examples are pretty boring. Not every criminal offense needs to be crazy or wacky but have fun and be creative with what you submit! It makes court more enticing and fun to play. Thank you!

items.title: Defendant
items.text: You've been sued or have committed a crime. Either way the defendant is the target of attention for any trial. Your role is to defend yourself with the help of your lawyer(s).

items.title: Court Intermission
items.text:
If you haven't already organized your thoughts and materials for the trial beforehand. The intermission is your time to do so. Regardless of if you're alone or accompanied by lawyers you need a game plan, evidence, and preperation.

How should I interact with my lawyers? However you want, obviously. But generally you should treat them well since your ability to win is dependent on them. Ensure that you're working with your lawyers than against.

items.title: Court Play Time
items.text: Don't say anything that might weaken your argument or get you incriminated. Rely on your lawyers as they're there to present you.

items.title: Judge
items.text: Your purpose is to ensure the trial goes smoothly. This page will serve as an all-in-one guide on how you can be a judge in Tucker Isles's Court party game!

items.title: Court Intermission
items.text:
During the Court's intermission is the best time to appoint your assistants for the trial.

What assistants are good to have?
  1. Time Keeper It's important to have someone keeping track of the time. This person needs to ensure that no round exceeds ten minutes long. If it does they need to alert the judge that the round's time has expired.
  2. Peace Keeper This person will yell at anyone that disrupts the fluency of the trial. They have the ability to mute any one person for three minutes every round.
Don't assistants seem like actual roles? They are official roles but are non-essential to the trial and instead are additive to spice up the trial.

With the rest of the time you have in intermission, keep a close eye on your DMs. It's not against the rules for any party of a trial to DM you in private.

items.title: Court Play Time
items.text:
You are the officiater for every round, and no round can proceed without your spoken or written initiation.

You are especially expected to listen for the majority of the trial. However you do bear spoken authority to a certain degree. In other words, you can inquire to the party that's arguing for that round (prioritized party), and if the opposing party says a callout like, (e.g.) "heresay" you can object to it and let the prioritized party continue.

items.title: Jury
items.text: The jury consists of all the spectators during the trial. The role of the jury is to pay attention to the trial, provide additional inquiries, and assist in determining the outcome of the trial.

items.title: Unique Sub-Roles
items.text:
Provided the trial's judge decides they want assistant(s), members of the jury can be selected for roles that increase the unpredictability and chaos of the trial.

Disclaimer

Please refer to this redirect to access the judge appointed sub-roles.

items.title: Lawyer
items.text: Whether you're representing a prosecutor or a defendant you're going to be arguing something. Your responsibility is to work with your client throughout the intermission and play time to ensure that your party wins.

items.title: Tips and Tricks
items.text: How to prepare evidence? Using a slideshow format is the ideal way to present evidence in Court. Most people will organize a quick Google slideshow for their evidence and present it. When can I edit my evidence presentation? Anytime! You are allowed to adjust and tweak your evidence presentation whenever needed. How do I talk to my party when the other party is presenting? I recommend creating a small group chat with your client and other lawyers. That way at any point during the trial you can reach out to them without interrupting or obstructing the proceeding of the trial.

items.title: Prosecutor
items.text: You're either a criminal prosecutor or someone suing another person. Either way your task it to punish the defendant for the alledged acts they've committed.

items.title: Court Intermission
items.text:
If you haven't already organized your thoughts and materials for the trial beforehand. The intermission is your time to do so. Regardless of if you're alone or accompanied by lawyer(s) you need a game plan, evidence, and preperation.

How should I interact with my lawyers? However you want, obviously. But generally you should treat them well since your ability to win is dependent on them. Ensure that you're working with your lawyer(s) than against.

items.title: Court Play Time
items.text: Don't say anything that might weaken your argument. Rely on your lawyer(s) as they're there to present you.
